title: Space Colony: Frontier Defense
description: Command your space colony's defense forces against an alien invasion on a distant planet. Deploy marines, engineers, and mechs to protect your commander and secure vital resource nodes before the alien swarm overwhelms you.
learning_objectives: Develop tactical positioning and spatial awareness
Build resilience through adaptive defense strategies

core_skills.name: Tactical Command
core_skills.description: Multi-step planning and defensive positioning (executive function)

core_skills.name: Threat Assessment
core_skills.description: Evaluating danger levels and committing resources (prospect theory)

core_skills.name: Resource Discipline
core_skills.description: Saving energy for critical moments vs immediate deployment (self-regulation)

core_skills.name: Battle Adaptation
core_skills.description: Adjusting formations to alien attack patterns (cognitive flexibility)

core_skills.name: Defensive Resolve
core_skills.description: Maintaining effective defense after unit losses (psychological resilience)

how_to_play: Click your blue colony units to select them
Green dots show valid movement positions
Red highlights mark alien units you can engage
Use the Mech's EMP Blast or Engineer's Shield to gain tactical advantage
Protect your Commander — if they fall, the colony is lost!
Reach 55 Energy or eliminate the Alien Queen to win!
Watch out for asteroid fields (blocked) and radiation zones (penalty)!

player_pieces.label: Commander
player_pieces.description: Colony Commander. If they fall, all is lost. Can rally nearby troops for enhanced movement.

player_pieces.label: Space Marine
player_pieces.description: Fast assault unit. Moves in cardinal directions with extended range.

player_pieces.label: Battle Mech
player_pieces.description: Heavy diagonal assault unit with ranged EMP capability.

player_pieces.label: Engineer
player_pieces.description: Support unit with short range but can move in all directions.

ai_pieces.label: Alien Queen
ai_pieces.description: The hive mind. Destroying her ends the invasion.

ai_pieces.label: Scout Drone
ai_pieces.description: Fast alien scout that moves in straight lines.

ai_pieces.label: Brute
ai_pieces.description: Heavy diagonal attacker. Slow but devastating.

ai_pieces.label: Swarmling
ai_pieces.description: Basic alien unit. Slow but numerous and persistent.

external_events.label: Solar Flare
external_events.narrative: A massive solar flare disrupts all electronic systems! All units lose mobility temporarily.

external_events.label: Emergency Supply Drop
external_events.narrative: Earth sends an emergency resupply! Colony forces gain enhanced mobility.

external_events.label: Gravity Anomaly
external_events.narrative: A gravity anomaly warps the battlefield! All units struggle to maintain formation.

move_tips.capture: Every alien neutralized secures the colony. In space defense, reducing threats systematically is better than reactive firefighting.
move_tips.resource: Controlling energy nodes powers your entire defense grid. In space exploration, sustainable energy infrastructure is the foundation of survival.
move_tips.objective: Securing key installations protects the colony core. In space defense, layered defense positions buy time and options.
move_tips.risk: Traversing hazardous zones drains energy but may reach critical objectives. In space, calculated risks are necessary when resources are finite.
move_tips.reward: Resource caches provide vital energy boosts. In space exploration, efficient resource discovery and collection determines colony viability.
move_tips.center: Controlling central positions gives defensive coverage in all directions. In space strategy, central positioning maximizes response flexibility.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Managing resources across multiple rounds to reach the best outcome
transfer_exercises.real_world: Planning study time over a semester rather than cramming before exams
transfer_exercises.challenge: Create a resource management plan for your next month: budget time/money/energy across competing priorities.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from negative events across game rounds
transfer_exercises.real_world: Maintaining performance after setbacks in a sports season or project
transfer_exercises.challenge: Track your energy/mood for 5 days. Notice patterns. What depletes you? What restores you?

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

reflection_prompt: Which move opened the board for you, and which closed your options? Why?
